system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Review of Seller’s Updated SPA & Disclosure Letter – Project Kestrel  
**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team  
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook (internal, unshared) vs. Seller’s “fair and balanced” positions  

---

### 1.  Executive Summary  
The Seller’s draft **systematically collapses every key protection in our playbook into a single, Seller-friendly general regime**.  The 20%/AUD 4.8 M cap, 18-month claim period, data-room/public-register deemed disclosure, blanket buyer-knowledge bar, and the merger of fundamental/title claims into the general cap are **not** “minor gaps”—they are a complete rewrite of the risk allocation we are authorised to accept.  None of the conditional fallbacks (20% cap, 18-month period) have been approved by Amelia Frost.  On Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, employee bonuses, and title evidence the Seller either kicks the can post-Completion or relies on internal, unverified records.  **We must issue a detailed mark-up reversing each departure and flagging the items that require principal-level sign-off before we can move forward.**

---

### 2.  Material Departures – Clause by Clause  

| # | Playbook Position | Seller Position | Why It Matters / Risk | Required Push-Back |
|---|-------------------|----------------|----------------------|-------------------|
| **1** | **General Cap: 25% / AUD 6 M** (20% / AUD 4.8 M **only** with Amelia Frost written authority – **none given**) | 20% / AUD 4.8 M (Clause 12.1) | We lose AUD 1.2 M of recovery headroom without any principal approval. | **Reject.** Restore 25% / AUD 6 M.  If Seller insists on 20%, obtain written Frost authority *before* counter-signing. |
| **2** | **De minimis AUD 5 K; Basket AUD 50 K (first-dollar recovery once exceeded)** | De minimis AUD 25 K; Basket AUD 250 K (excess-only recovery) (Clause 12.2) | 5× higher thresholds + “excess-only” means Seller bears **zero** liability for claims ≤ AUD 250 K and only marginal liability above. | **Reject.** Reinstate AUD 5 K / AUD 50 K first-dollar basket. |
| **3** | **General claims period: 24 months** (18 months fallback needs Frost approval – **none**) | 18 months (Clause 12.3/13) | Six months less discovery time; no principal sign-off. | **Reject.** Restore 24 months. |
| **4** | **Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥ 6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar** | Capacity & title warranties **subject to same caps, baskets, time limits as general warranties** (“administrative simplicity”) | Title/capacity defects (e.g., Seller doesn’t own 100% of shares) would be capped at AUD 4.8 M and time-barred at 18 months. | **Reject outright.** Separate regime mandatory.  No compromise on title/capacity. |
| **5** | **Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct: carved out of ALL caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non-reliance** | Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance apply to **“all Claims of any nature”** (Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Seller seeks to cap even fraud.  Unenforceable in NSW but creates litigation risk; plays into Seller’s “whole agreement” narrative. | **Red-line.** Insert express carve-out: “Nothing in this Agreement limits liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.” |
| **6** | **Disclosure: specific, fair disclosure only** – reject whole data-room, public registers, prudent search | **General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) + public registers + statutory registers** (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2) | Shifts burden to Buyer to find needles in haystack; “deemed knowledge” of 10,000+ pages. | **Reject.** Require schedule of *specific* disclosed matters (page/bates references).  Delete general disclosure clauses. |
| **7** | **Buyer knowledge: no blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity** | **Blanket bar** if Buyer or advisers “had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records” (Clause 8.3) | “Discoverable” = constructive knowledge of entire data room.  No named Seller knowledge persons.  No carve-outs. | **Delete Clause 8.3.**  If Seller insists on knowledge qualifier, limit to *actual* knowledge of named Buyer signatories + carve-outs per playbook. |
| **8** | **Bluefen: effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied *before* Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient** | **Reasonable endeavours only; consent “satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent”** – no evidence conditions (11.3) satisfied (Disclosure 2) | 30% revenue customer; change-control conditions (11.3) unmet.  Post-Completion consent failure = Buyer bears risk. | **Condition Precedent:** Bluefen written consent + certified copy of satisfied 11.3 conditions *must* be delivered at Completion.  No “reasonable endeavours” fallback. |
| **9** | **Riverlark: current payout from Completion funds + effective security releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval** | **Release “to be provided following Completion”** – no payout mechanism, no security discharge, no undertaking (Clause 2/7, Disclosure 3) | AUD 3.2 M debt + security remains on Target’s assets post-Completion.  Buyer funds Seller’s repayment risk. | **Funds-flow mandate:** Riverlark paid out *at* Completion from purchase price; security releases delivered *at* Completion.  If Seller insists on post-Completion, require irrevocable undertaking + Frost written approval. |
| **10** | **Employee bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420 K + on-costs as specific line item or Seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude** | **Not separately itemised in funds flow**; “matter for the Seller”; on-costs undisclosed (Disclosure 5, Seller Update) | AUD 420 K + payroll tax/super (~AUD 80–100 K) effectively deducted from equity value without transparency. | **Insert specific line item** in Completion accounts / funds flow for AUD 420 K + on-costs, payable by Seller or escrowed. |
| **11** | **Ironquay IP: broaden narrow SOW3 indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180 K not independently verified** | **Existing indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; “considered adequate”** (Clause 11.1, Disclosure 4) | AUD 180 K outstanding, no bank verification, no receipt/assignment in data room.  Narrow indemnity leaves IP ownership gap. | **Broaden indemnity** to cover IP ownership, third-party claims, and cure costs beyond SOW3 fees.  Require proof of payment/assignment before Completion. |
| **12** | **Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach** | **“Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material”** (Clause 4.6/Schedule 6) | Seller minimises; investigation incomplete.  No obligation to update Buyer post-signing. | **Specific indemnity + ongoing investigation covenant** (logs preserved, weekly updates, Buyer approval of any notification).  No assumption of non-materiality. |
| **13** | **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330 K): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction** | **“Ordinary-course operating costs”** (Disclosure 8) | Disclosure silent on whether unavoidable/terminable/accrued.  Could be hidden liability. | **Due diligence follow-up:** require Seller to confirm each renewal’s cancellability, accrual status, and whether any change-control triggers.  Reserve right to treat as Debt if not ordinary course. |
| **14** | **Tax / IP warranties: OPEN – no resolution, no unlimited liability assumed** | **“Considered settled under the general regime above”** (Seller Update) | Attempts to close open issues via general cap/basket/time-bar. | **Reject.**  Tax and IP warranties remain subject to separate negotiation; no deemed settlement. |
| **15** | **Title evidence: independent proof of ownership/encumbrances/authority; DD-012 register is internal, not independent** | **Title “evidenced by Company share register at DD-012”** (Disclosure 10, Seller Update) | Share register is self-serving; no ASIC search, no beneficial ownership confirmation, no encumbrance check. | **Require:** (a) current ASIC extract, (b) Seller solvency certificate, (c) no-encumbrance undertaking, (d) board resolutions authorising sale. |
| **16** | **Non-reliance / entire agreement: must not override fraud carve-out or specific indemnities** | **Applies to “all Claims of any nature”** (Clause 20.5) | Same issue as #5 – tries to fence out fraud/indemnity claims. | **Amend** to exclude fraud, specific indemnities, and fundamental warranties from non-reliance clause. |

---

### 3.  Disclosure Letter – Specific Red Flags  
| Disclosure | Issue | Action |
|------------|-------|--------|
| 1.1 / 1.2 | General disclosure of entire data room + public registers | **Delete.**  Insist on specific disclosure schedule. |
| 2 (Bluefen) | No final consent, no evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied | **Condition Precedent** (see #8 above). |
| 3 (Riverlark) | No repayment, no discharge | **Funds-flow payout + releases at Completion** (see #9). |
| 4 (Ironquay) | AUD 180 K open, no independent verification, no assignment | **Broaden indemnity + pre-Completion proof of payment/assignment** (see #11). |
| 5 (Bonuses) | AUD 420 K + on-costs absent from funds flow | **Specific line item / Seller-funded** (see #10). |
| 6 (Export) | Investigation preliminary; scope/access/notification unknown | **Indemnity + investigation covenant** (see #12). |
| 8 (Sandbar) | Three renewals AUD 330 K – no clarity on avoidability/accrual | **Seller certification** on each renewal’s status; reserve Debt treatment. |
| 10 (Title) | DD-012 internal register only | **Independent evidence package** (see #15). |
| 1.4 / 11 | “Nothing admits breach… Buyer must evaluate” | Standard reservation – no action needed but confirms Seller not conceding materiality. |

---

### 4.  Recommendations – Immediate Next Steps  

1. **Issue a comprehensive mark-up** of the SPA and Disclosure Letter reversing every departure
